key_findings.finding: The boronic ester partner `Cc1ccc2c(cnn2C2CCCCO2)c1B1OC(C)(C)C(C)(C)O1` is the stronger choice in the retrieved empirical records. With the exact heteroaryl triflate scaffold (or its positional isomer representation), the coupled product was reported at 98.6% and 97.2% yield at 100 °C for 1 h; a closely matching LiOtBu/DMF Suzuki record using this boronic ester gave 100.0% yield at 100 °C for 1 h. The product is the biaryl formed by replacing triflate-derived O/SO2CF3 leaving-group connectivity with the heteroaryl fragment from the boronic ester.

The potassium trifluoroborate partner `Cc1ccc2c(cnn2C2CCCCO2)c1[B-](F)(F)F.[K+]` gave the same coupled product in exact-triflate records at 84.6%, 84.5%, 83.7%, 83.1%, and lower values down to 80.7%, all at 100 °C for 1 h. These records used fluoride-containing or other inorganic activators rather than the specified LiOtBu condition.

On the retrieved evidence, select the pinacol boronic ester rather than the potassium trifluoroborate: it shows an approximate 13–15 percentage-point yield advantage in matched exact-triflate records (98.6–97.2% versus 84.6–83.1% for the highest BF3K records), with additional close records supporting 100% under LiOtBu/DMF. The database does not provide a directly head-to-head record with every stated component, so the precise yield under the ferrocenyl-phosphine/LiOtBu/DMF combination remains an expectation rather than a directly measured value.
